name: Sterling-Nakamura Legal Override Pistol LOP-1 'Compliance'
description: A sidearm that fires coded RF rounds which, upon penetrating the skin, broadcast an override signal to the target's neural interface that triggers a mandatory system lockdown. The lockdown disables voluntary motor control for 60 seconds while broadcasting the target's identity, location, and biometric status to law enforcement networks. Sterling-Nakamura developed it under contract with GLMZ governance bodies as a 'lawful compliance enforcement tool' — it is essentially a gun that arrests people by hijacking their cyberware. The round's RF signal uses an encryption key that only law enforcement neural interfaces can revoke, making the lockdown non-negotiable. Unaugmented individuals are unaffected by the RF component and experience only a low-velocity impact bruise.
specifications:
caliber: 6mm RF-coded compliance round
muzzle velocity: 120 m/s — subcutaneous embedding
magazine: 12 rounds
effective range: 5-25 meters
lockdown duration: 60 seconds
motor control override: Full voluntary motor suppression
identity broadcast: Automatic to law enforcement networks
effect on unaugmented: Bruise-level impact only
weight: 0.8 kg
story_hooks: Black market LOP-1 rounds have been reprogrammed to broadcast a different identity than the target's — someone is using compliance rounds to frame innocent people for crimes.
A vulnerability in the compliance signal encryption has been discovered that allows any RF transmitter to trigger the 60-second lockdown — every augmented person in GLMZ is potentially vulnerable.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, angular sidearm with an aggressive forward-swept design. The barrel is noticeably recessed into the slide, giving it a compressed, purposeful appearance. Twin RF antenna nodes flank the muzzle, creating a distinctive forked profile. The overall impression is clinical and authoritarian—form follows function with zero concession to aesthetics.
physical_description.dimensions: Length: 18.5 cm | Height: 12 cm | Width: 3.2 cm | Barrel length: 8.5 cm (recessed)
physical_description.weight_description: Surprisingly light and balanced, with forward weighting from the antenna assembly. Sits confidently in the palm without fatigue—designed for extended duty wear
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polymer composite frame with steel slide and breech block. Antenna nodes are brushed titanium-alloy
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal polymer with satin-finish steel accents. The antenna nodes catch light distinctly—intentionally visible to signal authority
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal black with steel-gray slide. Accent: electric blue RF indicator LED on the left side of the frame (active when charged)
physical_description.grip_texture: Deeply textured polymer grip with subtle grip-angle ergonomics. Friction-optimized for gloved hands—wet, synthetic, or reinforced
distinctive_features: Dual RF antenna nodes flanking the muzzle in fork configuration
Small LED status indicator (blue = armed/active) on left frame
Recessed barrel with visible RF coil housing beneath slide
Encrypted serial plate on right side with GLMZ governance authorization stamp
Magazine well has faint haptic feedback ridges for blind magazine changes
Slide has micro-etched 'COMPLIANCE ENFORCEMENT' text along top
Grip safety integrated with network handshake sensor
Heat sink ridges on slide (RF broadcasting generates minimal thermal signature)
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Sterling-Nakamura logo (interlocking S-N) on left side of slide. Authorization stamp from GLMZ Law Enforcement Commission on rear grip panel. Serial number plate below slide on right frame with QR code for law enforcement network validation
physical_description.condition_typical: Meticulously maintained—field-issued sidearms are regularly cleaned and RF-calibrated. Will show minor holster wear on the right side but no visible damage. Battery indicator on grip is frequently checked. Antenna nodes are inspected for micro-fractures
